'''Aleksandar Nikola Donev''' (November 1979 – November 2023) was an American and Macedonian applied mathematician who worked on [[scientific computing]], [[fluid dynamics]], mathematical [[materials science]] and [[computational biology]]. He was a professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], [[New York University]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=39yX_hQAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Aleksandar Donev|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

== Background ==
Donev grew up in [[Veles]], Socialist Republic of Macedonia. At age 17 he began studies at the [[State University of New York at Plattsburgh]], a small town in northern New York State. He soon transferred to [[Michigan State University]] in East Lansing from where he graduated at the top of his class in Physics. He earned a Ph.D. degree in Applied and Computational Mathematics from [[Princeton University]] in 2006 under the guidance of [[Salvatore Torquato]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy | id= 177216 | name= Aleksandar Donev}}</ref> His thesis work concerned packing of hard elliptical particles.<ref> {{Cite journal |title=Improving the density of jammed disordered packings using ellipsoids |vauthors=Donev A, Cisse I, Sachs D, Variano EA, Stillinger FH, Connelly R, Torquato S, Chaikin PM|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14963324/ |date=2004-02-13 |journal=Science |pages=990–993}}
</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1= Donev|first1= A.|last2= Stillinger|first2= F. H.|last3= Chaikin|first3= P. M.|last4= Torquato|first4= S.|url= https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.255506&hl=en|title= Unusually dense crystal packings of ellipsoids|journal= Physical Review Letters|date= 2004|volume= 92|issue= 25 Pt 1|article-number= 255506|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.255506|pmid= 15245027|arxiv= cond-mat/0403286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021999104003146&hl=en|title=Neighbor list collision-driven molecular dynamics simulation for nonspherical hard particles. I. Algorithmic details. A Donev, S Torquato, FH Stillinger. Journal of Computational Physics 202 (2), pg. 737-764 (2005)}}</ref>

He was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[Lawrence Livermore Laboratory]] and later won the [[Luis W. Alvarez]] Postdoctoral Fellowship to work at the [[Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]]. In 2010 Donev joined the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], [[New York University]] as faculty.{{cn|date=April 2026}}

Donev died on November 2023 before the age of 45. He is mourned by family, friends, students, colleagues and collaborators.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cims.nyu.edu/dynamic/news/1443/&hl=en|title=Obituary of Professor Aleksandar N. Donev (1979–2023)}}</ref>

== Research ==
Donev worked on [[Scientific Computing]], [[Computational Mathematics]] and particularly for his work on Fluctuating Hydrodynamics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epubs.siam.org/action/cookieAbsent|title=The Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|website=The Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|doi=10.1137/120864520&hl=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pubs.aip.org/aip/jcp/article/142/22/224107/564533&hl=en|title=Fluctuating hydrodynamics of multi-species reactive mixtures. AK Bhattacharjee, K Balakrishnan, AL Garcia, JB Bell, A Donev. The Journal of chemical physics 142 (22) (2015).}}</ref> and numerical methods for suspensions in Stokes flow and complex fluids.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/090774501&hl=en|title= A hybrid particle-continuum method for hydrodynamics of complex fluids. A Donev, JB Bell, AL Garcia, BJ Alder. Multiscale Modeling & Simulation 8 (3), 871-911 (2010).|doi= 10.1137/090774501}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://msp.org/camcos/2016/11-1/p04.xhtml&hl=en|title=An immersed boundary method for rigid bodies. B Kallemov, A Bhalla, B Griffith, A Donev. Communications in Applied Mathematics and Computational Science 11 (1), pg.79-141 (2016).}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://msp.org/camcos/2016/11-2/p04.xhtml/&hl=en|title=Hydrodynamics of suspensions of passive and active rigid particles: a rigid multiblob approach. F Balboa Usabiaga, B Kallemov, B Delmotte, A Bhalla, B Griffith, A Donev. Communications in Applied Mathematics and Computational Science 11 (2), pg. 217-296 (2017).}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://journals.aps.org/prfluids/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevFluids.6.014102&hl=en|title= Integral-based spectral method for inextensible slender fibers in Stokes flow.O Maxian, A Mogilner, A Donev. Physical Review Fluids 6 (1), 014102 (2021).|doi= 10.1103/PhysRevFluids.6.014102|arxiv= 2007.11728}}</ref> He worked on modeling the effect of thermal noise in physical systems, particularly gasses, liquids, colloids and cross linked networks of actin filaments and related applications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nphys3970&hl=en|title=Unstable fronts and motile structures formed by microrollers. M Driscoll, B Delmotte, M Youssef, S Sacanna, A Donev, P Chaikin. Nature Physics 13 (4), pg.375-379 (2016)}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1= Yang|first1= T.|last2= Sprinkle|first2= B.|last3= Guo|first3= Y.|last4= Qian|first4= J.|last5= Hua|first5= D.|last6= Donev|first6= A.|author7= Marr DWM|last8= Wu|first8= N.|title= Reconfigurable microbots folded from simple colloidal chains.
